latest_release.body:
### Added

- **Folder workspaces.** Run your project’s tests in a terminal and try the app in a browser while your chat stays open beside them. Choose the computer and project directory once for the folder. Even in a shared folder, everyone can return to their own tabs and layout. If you used the standalone Open WebUI Computer (cptr) app, that workflow is now built into Open WebUI. [#34804](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34804), [#34805](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34805), [#34800](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34800), [#34803](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34803)
- **Project instructions and skills.** Tell the assistant how your project works once in an `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` file. Every new chat in that project folder reads those instructions. Connect the project machine with Open Terminal 0.18.0 or later and the assistant can also follow reusable project instructions called skills, run checks in your terminal and inspect the result in your browser tab.
- **Long chat performance.** Sending a message was 34× faster in our 130 MB PostgreSQL test chat. The server accepted it in 0.32 seconds, down from 10.9, because it now saves just the messages that changed. Database writes fell from 533 MB to 2 KB per message. [#34689](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34689), [#34671](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34671), [#34688](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34688), [#34672](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34672), [#34674](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34674), [#34670](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34670), [#34646](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34646)
- **Automatic model selection.** Put one router in the chat’s model picker and it can send coding questions to one model and writing requests to another. Admins choose text patterns or describe the kind of question each model should handle. If nothing matches, the router uses the first model on its list or picks one at random. [#34900](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34900), [#34895](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34895), [#34791](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34791), [#34796](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34796), [#34908](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34908), [#34662](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34662), [#34956](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34956), [#34957](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34957), [#34887](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34887), [#34786](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34786), [#34793](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34793), [#34897](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34897), [#34898](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34898), [#34466](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/34466), [#15996](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/15996)
- **Citations beside the chat.** Hover over a source number for a quick excerpt, or click it to read the evidence beside the answer. You can compare passages from the same document, see how closely they match your question and jump to the cited PDF page when page information is available. [#34923](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34923), [#34836](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/34836), [#34921](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34921), [#34828](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34828), [#34831](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34831), [#34832](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34832), [#34833](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34833), [#34913](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34913), [#34834](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34834), [#34829](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34829), [#20829](htt

detail.readme:
Open WebUI

Open WebUI is a home for AI: an extensible, easy-to-use, self-hosted platform built to run entirely offline. Connect local models through Ollama, use OpenAI-compatible APIs for local and cloud models, or add agents through Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

With uv installed (macOS/Linux) DATA_DIR=~/.open-webui uvx --python 3.12 open-webui@latest serve # Or install and run with pip (Python 3.12) pip install open-webui open-webui serve ``` Then open [http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080). #### Docker ```bash docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main ``` Then open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). | Image tag | Includes | | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `:main` | Standard image with local AI dependencies | | `:slim` | Lightweight image using external services for embeddings, document extraction, and voice | | `:cuda` | Open WebUI with CUDA acceleration | | `:ollama` | Open WebUI bundled with Ollama | | `:dev` | Latest development build | Add these options to `docker run` before the image name as needed: | Option | Purpose | | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `-e OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://your-ollama-server:11434` | Connect to Ollama on another server | | `-e OPENAI_API_KEY=your_secret_key` | Set your OpenAI API key | | `-e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` | Disable Hugging Face model downloads for offline use | | `--gpus all` | Enable Nvidia GPU access for `:cuda` or `:ollama`; requires the Nvidia Container Toolkit | See the [Docker installation guide](https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/) for setup instructions and configuration options. #### Desktop App [Download the native desktop app](https://github.com/open-webui/desktop) for macOS, Windows, and Linux. [Read the docs →](https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/) ### Ecosystem - [Open Terminal](https://github.com/open-webui/open-terminal) / [Terminals (Enterprise)](https://github.com/open-webui/terminals): The action layer that turns Open WebUI into a full agent harness, with enterprise orchestration for per-user workspaces. - [Knowledge Base Sync (oikb)](https://github.com/open-webui/oikb): Mirror folders, repos, buckets, and wikis into Open WebUI Knowledge Bases with incremental sync. - [Open WebUI Computer](https://github.com/open-webui/computer): Your computer in any browser: files, editor, terminal, git, and optional AI agents, running on your real machine. See the [ecosystem documentation](https://docs.openwebui.com/ecosystem/) for details. ### Troubleshooting and Updates See the [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.openwebui.com/troubleshooting/) for connection issues and the [updating guide](https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/updating) to update your installation. ### Documentation See the [docs](https://docs.openwebui.com/) for configuration and usage, and the [roadmap](https://docs.openwebui.com/roadmap/) for planned work. For Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and other setups, see the [installation docs](https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/). ### Support [Open an issue](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues) or [start a discussion](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions). Find us on [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenWebUI/), [X](https://x.com/OpenWebUI), and [Discord](https://discord.gg/5rJgQTnV4s). ### Security Report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/security). Security reports are accepted only through GitHub. ### Star History #### License Includes code under the Open WebUI License, which requires preserving the Open WebUI branding, and prior contributions under their original licenses.
